brief.reader:
Selected audience: Indie SaaS founder/maker creating launch & demo videos.
Research context describes some members of this market, not this recipient's installed tools or experiences. Follow the campaign request when it scopes the job.
Observed situation (grounded; check applicability): Indie and solo SaaS founders preparing a Product Hunt launch build their own launch/demo video and page assets as part of the process, often alongside writing descriptions and filling out their product page before going live.

brief.promise: Screen Studio lets a Mac-based founder record a product walkthrough, apply cursor effects after recording, and export the result at up to 4K and 60 fps.
brief.orientation: Screen Studio is a macOS screen recorder that a solo founder uses to record a product walkthrough and get a polished demo video out of it without doing manual video editing.
brief.arc: In one email, move the reader from knowing that Screen Studio is another screen recorder to understanding its specific value for a product walkthrough, then invite them to try that workflow on a Mac.
brief.sequence_rationale: One email should carry one complete product-led argument: Screen Studio records synchronized mouse-movement data and adds the cursor back afterward, giving a founder post-recording control over cursor effects before a high-resolution export. This is more persuasive and better supported than leading with price, privacy, or a broad speed claim. The CTA is the smallest documented adoption step, while the copy must not imply a free trial or guaranteed production time. The single thing the user could send us that would most change this campaign is a readable copy of the missing Screen Studio source material, or verification of its missing details.
